newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Ethiopian Marxists killed the educated, trial told.
newsitem.headline: Ethiopian Marxists killed the educated, trial told.

text.p: Ethiopia's former Marxist rulers made a deliberate effort to destroy educated people in the country, a witness said in a genocide trial on Tuesday.
The witness was testifying at the trial of 71 former Ethiopian Marxist officials accused of genocide and crimes against humanity. All 71 could be sentenced to death if found guilty.
"I am of the opinion that killings undertaken by the Dergue, the miltitary junta in Ethiopia, were aimed at a brain destruction," the 67-year-old witness, a former educator, told the court.
Under court rules, the witness cannot be named.

Only 46 of the 71 former military junta known as the "Dergue" were in the dock on Tuesday. The other 25 including dictator Mengistu Haile Mariam who ruled Ethiopia from 1977 to 1991 are being tried in absentia.
Mengistu now lives in exile in Zimbabwe after fleeing the country in May 1991 shortly before rebels entered the capital and set up a new government.

The witness told the court: "I had conducted studies about the killings and the conclusion I reached was that almost all those young men and women executed by the Dergue were successful students in their fields of competence -- it was a brain destruction."

He said in 1975 armed men went to his residence and took two of his children to jail after ransacking the house. They returned for a second time the next day and also took him with them. He was released after a spell of some 10 days in prison.

But his two children, Markos Tedla, a second year engineering student, and Abraham Tedla, a high school student, were sentenced to two years in prison on charges of belonging to a rival Marxist group.

The witness said his two children were taken to a central investigation office after inmates in the country's main prison went on hunger strike. His younger son was returned to prison to complete his term but the elder one, Markos, did not return and was executed by the Dergue.

A 37-year-old secretary who also appeared in court as a witness for the prosecution said she was taken from her office in 1981 by armed men and was continuously tortured at the central investigation office to force her to admit that she belonged to a rebel Marxist group.

Ethiopia's new government has charged 5,198 people with war crimes, aggravated homicide and genocide. Of these 1,200 are suspected of involvement in the "Red Terror" campaign during Mengistu's 17-year rule.
Death squads in the 1977-78 campaign hunted down thousands from rival Marxist groups and other opposition organisations on behalf of the Dergue.
The trial was adjourned until Thursday.
